## Claimed and dispatched

- **Session**: `session_01W6HFzyH98W1YaQXhJUJt6o` (seat post #6367)
- **Branch**: `claude/issue-12032-autorestart-never-reinits`
- Comments re-read in the same action as the claim: one, the triage seat's blocker-resolution and grading. No prior claim by any other session.

**Blocker discharged, verified rather than inherited**: #11825 is closed via merged PR #12336, ruling **ADR-0049 route 2** — the authorable `AdvancedPluginLifecycleConfig` surface is retired, and the lifecycle classes stay as a **kept host-driven library**. So the card's own "triage after #11825 settles" condition is answered, and answered in the direction that keeps this live: `PluginHealthMonitor` remains published and hand-drivable, which makes a destroy-without-`init()` "restart" that ends at `healthy` a defect in a shipped library rather than a defect in something on its way out.

**Serial check**: lands in `packages/core/src/health-monitor.ts`. The two sibling cards in this module family are on different files — #12428 / PR #12571 is on `hot-reload.ts`, #12397 / PR #12581 is in objectql. No overlap, no hold.

Triage's three dispatch notes go to the dev intact, including the one that sets the bar: **a loud "destroy-only, will not re-init" posture is acceptable; a silent `healthy` after destroy is not.** The remedy fork (implement a real restart through a host-provided re-init hook, versus stop claiming a restart) is the dev's to answer against what a host *can* provide post-#12336 — and the surrounding precedent is strong and recent: #12340 and #12428 both took "keep the class, stop the lie" in this same library, today.

Also carried: re-take the spec/docs citations on the post-#12336 ref before quoting them. That PR rewrote the lifecycle spec and docs surface, so the card's `plugin-lifecycle-advanced.zod.ts` describe-string and `plugin-lifecycle-advanced.mdx:114` references may have moved or gone. The library defect stands either way — but a PR quoting a line that no longer exists is a PR nobody can check.

## Notes for the reviewer

**Route, in one line**: the fork resolved to *stop claiming a restart*, and the measurement that decided it is that `ObjectKernel.context` is `private` and `KernelBase.createContext()` is `protected` — so a host-provided re-init hook has nothing to call, and route 1 would have meant building a per-plugin re-init kernel API for a caller that does not exist.

**The bar**: triage set it at *"a loud destroy-only, will not re-init posture is acceptable; a silent `healthy` after destroy is not."* This clears it from above — there is no destroy at all, because a half-restart turns a degraded plugin into a dead one the host still owns, and because destroy-only would have left `maxRestartAttempts` provably inert (a fresh ADR-0049 violation inside a PR retiring one).

**Citations re-taken**, as instructed: the `.zod.ts` describe-string survived #12336 unchanged; `plugin-lifecycle-advanced.mdx:114` **moved to line 66** and that page is now auto-generated; and the citation the card did not have — `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx:737` — was the hand-written page *teaching* the false contract, now corrected.

**CI status at report time**: `in_progress` — reported at draft-PR time per the dispatch contract, not after CI convergence.
